name: TinyLaunch
tagline: A paid launch platform where indie makers list products for exposure, badges and backlinks.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified. Listing fees are typically one-time per launch rather than a subscription.

verdictSummary: The software here is a directory with a submission form, a voting widget and a badge image endpoint. An agent can clone that in an afternoon and it will be completely worthless, because nobody visits your directory. What you are actually buying is a slot in front of an existing audience of makers plus a link from a domain that search engines already know about. No amount of local code manufactures either. The only honest DIY play is tooling around launches, not a launch platform of your own.
coreLoopDIY: A local dashboard that tracks which launch directories you have submitted to, when, what tier you paid for, and whether your backlink is actually live.
requirements: Your own list of launch directories and submission URLs
Outbound network access for the backlink checker
whatYouLose: The audience: a launch page with zero visitors is just a database row
Domain authority, which is the actual product when people buy listings for SEO
The badge that other makers recognise, since a badge you minted yourself signals nothing
Front page placement and the traffic spike on launch day
Being discovered by people browsing for new tools rather than looking for you
moatNotes: Two-sided and self-reinforcing: makers pay because visitors are there, visitors are there because makers keep launching. The backlink value is a side effect of years of accumulated crawl history.
whyPeopleStillPay: Launch directories are cheap, one-time, and boring in the best way: you pay a small fee, you get a listing, a badge and a link from a domain search engines already trust. That is a distribution purchase, not a software purchase. The build cost of the underlying site is close to zero, which is exactly why competing on features is pointless and why the incumbents that got early attention keep the pricing power. You are renting other people's attention for an afternoon.
notes: The directory is a weekend build; the audience is not. The moat is a two-sided network plus years of crawled domain authority, neither of which ships with your repo.
prompt:
Build a local launch tracker called "LaunchLedger". It is a personal dashboard for tracking submissions to startup launch directories. It is NOT a directory of its own.

Stack, no substitutions:
- Next.js 15 App Router, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS
- SQLite via better-sqlite3, file at ./data/launchledger.db
- Runs with `npm run dev` on localhost, single user, no auth, no accounts, no telemetry, no cloud

Data model:
- product: id, name, url, tagline
- directory: id, name, submitUrl, listingFeeCents, notes
- submission: id, productId, directoryId, status (planned | submitted | live | rejected), tier (free | paid), paidCents, submittedOn, listingUrl, lastCheckedAt, backlinkFound (bool), httpStatus

Features, in scope:
1. CRUD for products, directories and submissions, plain server actions and forms. No modal library.
2. Seed the directory table from ./seed/directories.json. Ship the file with 12 real placeholder rows I can edit by hand: name, submitUrl, empty notes. Do not hardcode fees.
3. A backlink checker: a POST route that fetches each submission's listingUrl server side, records httpStatus, and sets backlinkFound true if the raw HTML contains the product's domain. Follow up to 3 redirects, 10s timeout, 1 request per second sequential, custom User-Agent from env.
4. Dashboard: table of submissions grouped by product, colour coded status, total spend in dollars, count of live listings, count of live listings where backlinkFound is false. That last number is the point of the app.
5. CSV export of all submissions.

Out of scope, do not build: public pages, voting, badges, embeds, email, analytics, multi-user, Docker, any hosted deploy.

Details: secrets and config in .env.example only (USER_AGENT, CHECK_CONCURRENCY). Seed script `npm run seed`. Include a README with setup in under 10 lines and one sentence stating this tool tracks launches and does not generate traffic.
